title: TJM F30 Cluster
description: Instrument cluster themes after the F-series 6WB look: Comfort, Sport and Eco Pro, following the drive mode

de.bmw.infotainment.fasus.FASuS._optional: the NEXT limit ahead, not the one in force; not drawn yet, read for calibration

de.bmw.dass.settingsdriverassistancefunc._optional: the driver's OWN speed-limit settings, so our red arc follows the car's excess-speed display instead of our own guess. SUBSCRIBE ONLY, and that is not a style choice: all six are "rws" in the car's catalogue, but every one of their getters is {"id": 0}, and MainApp's IFConfigGenerator tests that id for truthiness. A zero reads as absent, so an "r" flag here makes the install fail with "Requested read for settingOffsetSpeed but no getter available", which the Store only ever shows as UPDATE_FAILED. That is what blocked 0.7.16 on the car four times; 0.7.17 dropped the "r". The notifiers are real (32789 and its neighbours), so the values still arrive, and with no "w" the app still cannot write a driver-assistance setting even by mistake. Checking that a getter EXISTS is not enough - check that its id is non-zero.

Both look for the signal behind BMW's warning / 'i' marker (config.ccMarker stays null).

de.bmw.infotainment.checkcontrol.CheckCo._probes: 0.7.18 diagnostics, READ ONLY and LOG ONLY (shared/hud.js 'probes' block): the stored check-control list (serviceId 46412, instance 1; getter 1, notifier 32769), logged once per change as ccmId, reason (CCM_SHOWN_BY_IC ...) and activeState only. settings.label: BMW's G20 round our dials (Comfort)
settings._about: The see-through look: our dials are drawn over BMW's own cluster, so BMW's bottom row, map and signs show between and under them (what the themes '6WB Dials + G20' and '6WB Sport + G20' used to be). ONLY 6WB Comfort has a see-through variant (hud/layouts/wb_dials.json): with this on, 6WB Sport and 6WB Eco Pro stay opaque, which is why the label says Comfort. MUST stay a bool: hud.js _toggleOn reads a plain key as 'on unless false', so a choice would read as always on.

settings.label: Bottom row while G20 shows
settings._about: ONE switch for the whole of BMW's bottom row (the owner, 2026-11-15: 'all6WB vs allG20'), in place of the seven own* settings of package F (ownRange / ownClock / ownTemp / ownNav / ownSign / ownInfo and the broken ownAll). 'all6WB': the range, the clock, the outside temperature, the road label, the speed-limit sign and the check-control message are all drawn by us, in the 6WB style; 'allG20': BMW draws all of them. The clock is ours only once a time zone is known (the 'timeZone' setting, the car's own zone or config.utcOffsetMinutes) - without one the head unit runs on UTC and only BMW's clock is right, which is what the retired ownClock 'auto' did. IT ONLY MEANS ANYTHING WHILE THE 'g20' TOGGLE SHOWS A SEE-THROUGH LAYOUT: in the opaque themes our own background covers BMW's row, so the row is always ours there and menu.js hides this one (config.menu.hideRowUnlessG20). NO 'reset' HERE: a reset would throw the migrated value away (kit/runtime/mgu.js:105-108). hud.js _rowFail still wins over this: an element whose signal is missing or whose drawing throws hands itself back to BMW whatever this says.
settings._packageX: 2026-11-16 (docs/strip/X-REPORT.md): 'all6WB' is ALL OR NOTHING. The whole row is ours, or the whole row is BMW's: when any one item cannot be drawn (a field missing, a message that cannot be read, a character the font lacks, a drawing that throws) the WHOLE row goes back to BMW until the app restarts, logged once with the reason. The row is also BMW's, without a latch, in standby (P with the engine off), while no time zone is known (the clock is always ours in all6WB: the car's own zone, config.clock, first) and until the car's check-control message has been read once. A BMW warning is never covered unless our own text for it has been on its way to the screen for 150 ms (hud.js _ccOpen).

settings.label: Our message's look (all ours)
settings._about: Package X (the owner, 2026-11-16): our check-control message is our own design, one short line - the headline only - in the road label's slot, drawn while the bottom row is 'all6WB'. A: a severity marker (a warning triangle for a red, yellow or orange message, an 'i' otherwise, in the car's own colour) before the headline, no frame. B: the same headline with a hairline above it and a segment in the severity's colour under it, no marker. Changes no layer (hud.js ROW_KEYS): the line is repainted. Inert while the row is BMW's.

settings.label: Red arc over the speed limit

waze.comment: Show Waze map inside the theme (shared/waze.js): waze-on-cluster's status file (read every second) and its control socket (one short 'start' command, then closed). Paths from waze-on-cluster 0.9.3.

config._comment: target panel: the whole 1920x720 instrument cluster, drawn over BMW's gauges. socketPath: cluster-render's documented default. location and utcOffsetMinutes: as in HUD Widgets (the clock box). tankLitres: the fuel gauge's full mark (the car sends litres, not the tank size; a G01 X3 holds 65). engine: the peak crank torque (Nm) and power (kW) the {{torquePct}} and {{powerPct}} tokens count from (an M40i: 500 Nm, 285 kW / 382 hp).

dme.comment: Boost from the engine unit (DME, ecu 18) over read-only UDS 0x22, only while the sport display sends no boost and a boost readout is shown. Absolute kPa, the outside air pressure (baro) is subtracted. Candidates tried in order, the first plausible one wins. From cauliflowermossgrape's car_vitals (MIT). Intake air temperature the same way (config.dme.intake, every 2 s, only while an intake readout shows); candidates from cruzen991/Cluster's signal table (MIT), unverified on this car.

boost.note: OBD PID 0x70 boost pressure control: actual boost pressure sensor A (absolute), 1/32 kPa
OBD PID 0x87 intake manifold absolute pressure sensor A, 1/32 kPa
OBD PID 0x0B intake manifold absolute pressure, kPa (max 255 = 1.5 bar boost)

baro.note: OBD PID 0x33 barometric pressure, kPa (101.3 when not available)

intake.note: OBD PID 0x0F intake air temperature, C + 40
OBD PID 0x77 charge air cooler temperature, bank 1 sensor 1 (byte after the support byte), C + 40

config._retiredSettings: 2026-11-15, the owner ("ці сетінги не мають сенсу"): the settings units / clock / timeZone / tankLitres / redline / shiftBefore were removed from the screen. They were leftovers from the generic gauge app - on an F30 theme the CAR is the authority for every one of them. What each falls back to now: units is always metric (its drop-down had a single option, "metric", so nothing is lost); the clock is 24-hour (config.clock24); the time zone comes from the car alone (config.clock, no manual override left); the tank is config.tankLitres above; the redline and the shift point are the two keys below. hud.js reads them through _redline() / _shiftBefore() / _clock24(), each of which still prefers a setting IF one exists, so re-adding any of these to "settings" brings the control straight back with no other change.

msa._from: audit/features, from the car's own catalogue (/etc/oap/someip/someip-interfaces.json, StatusConditionMSA). Flag s: notifier only, so the first value comes with the first change. The raw value is logged once per new value ('msa raw: ... -> ...'); check it on the car at a start/stop stop, with the MSA button off, and with a cold engine.

dayNight._from: fix/colour-daynight, from the car's catalogue (reference/car/2026-11-15/someip/someip-interfaces.json): Vehicle (service 46352, instance 1) field statusDayNightChangeOver, getter 19, notifier 32787, struct StatusDayNightChangeOverWrapper { dayNightChangeOver: enum DayNightChangeOver (default 3), destinationLCDLuminance, dampingLCDLuminance }. DayNightChangeOver: 0 KEINE_AENDERUNG (no change: the last day/night the car gave holds; none yet: the sun), 1 TAG (day), 2 NACHT (night), 3 SIGNAL_UNGUELTIG (invalid: the sun). Any other value counts as invalid. The meaning of 0 is read off its German name only and is UNCONFIRMED on the car. 'codes' turns an enum NAME back into its number for the log (numbers only). hud.js _isNight.

clock._about: The car's own time-zone offset, so our clock is right without the manual timeZone setting (the owner, 2026-11-15; the head unit itself runs on UTC). Package X (2026-11-16): THIS IS THE FIRST SOURCE; the timeZone setting (if a build still has it) and config.utcOffsetMinutes are the fallbacks, in that order. A decoded offset is taken only if it is a whole number of quarter hours within +-14 h; anything else is logged once as 'clock: the car's offset decodes to N minutes ... ignored' and the next source is used. The line to check on the car: 'clock: ours shows HH:MM, UTC+hh:mm from ...' - it must read what the head unit's own clock reads.
clock._confirm: STILL AN UNCONFIRMED ENCODING, now LIVE. The catalogue says timeZonesOffsetAutomaticallyUTC is a UInt8 but not what one step is; "factor" 15 (quarter hours) is a guess. It was only parsed and logged while the manual "timeZone" setting existed; the owner retired that setting on 2026-11-15 ("забираємо все, можемо покластися на машину"), so the car's value is now the ONLY source our clock has and "confirm" is true. It could not be settled off the car: the 2026-11-15 snapshot has no captured value, and timeDateUTC's other members carry UTC, not local time, so there is nothing to difference against. THE FAILURE MODE IS A VISIBLY WRONG CLOCK, nothing worse, and one glance at the car settles it: compare our clock with BMW's own. If ours is out by a whole number of hours, the step is wrong - set "factor" to 1 (minutes), 30 (half hours) or 60 (hours) so the logged line 'clock: the car's offset would be N minutes' reads the real offset. If it is out by a constant that is not a multiple of the step, use "offsetBy" (subtracted from the raw first).
clock._log: fix/cclist (0.7.19): 0.7.18's 'clock raw:' line was cut at 100 characters, just before the three zone members, and repeated every 10 s (the seconds change). Now the WHOLE struct (all ten members of TimeDateUTCWrapper) is logged, uncut, once per change of the members named in logOn only. On the owner's car (2026-11-17) statusClockTimeDateUTC read UHRZEIT_UEBER_UTC_VERFUEGBAR_UND_UEBER_QUARZ_WEITERGEZAEHLT_OFFSETS_NICHT_VERFUEGBAR (the catalogue enum, value 3: 'UTC available, counted on by the quartz, OFFSETS NOT AVAILABLE') - the car itself says this struct carries no offset, so config.clockLocal below is what gives the zone there. The factor (15) is NOT changed: there is still no evidence for any step.

clockLocal._about: fix/cclist (0.7.19): the time zone's FALLBACK after config.clock (hud.js _tzSource): the local time the cluster shows, KombiIF statusShowTimeDate (ShowTimeDateWrapper displayHour / displayMinute; getter 30, notifier 32798), against the head unit's own UTC clock, rounded to 15 minutes (hud.js tzOf kind 'local'). An hour or minute out of range (the catalogue default 255) gives none. UNCONFIRMED on the car: that this field reaches the head unit, and that it carries LOCAL time (its sibling DisplayStatus.TimeDate is the same struct). The line to check: 'clock (local) raw: {...} -> 120' and 'clock: ours shows HH:MM, UTC+02:00 from the car's shown clock'. Set to null to drop it.

_bottomRow.about: Package 'bottom row' (docs/BOTTOM-ROW-PACKAGE.md). The three shapes below name the car's own fields for the speed-limit sign, the check-control message and the road label, verified member by member against the car's catalogue (reference/car/2026-11-15/someip/someip-interfaces.json, 2026-11-15). Each is OPTIONAL: set it to null and nothing is subscribed and nothing changes. WHAT IS DRAWN is decided by the one setting "bottomRow", which is "allG20" by default, so the car draws all three until the owner picks "all6WB" (it replaced the seven own* settings, 2026-11-15). Every new raw combination is logged ONCE as a SHAPE: the message text, the road name and the position are personal data and never reach the log.
_bottomRow.calibrate: On the car, watch for the log lines 'sign: ...', 'check-control message: ...', 'road label: ...', 'navigation: ...' and 'position: ...'. They say which enum values and lengths the car really sends; correct the maps below from them.
_bottomRow.signShape: { iface, field, invalidPath + invalidOn, valuePath, factor, min, max, unitPath + mph + noUnit, none / end / unknown (raw speed values), warnPath + warnMap, suppPath + suppMap, stylePath + styleMap, surePath + sureOn, npPath + npMap, npDistPath }: shared/hud.js signOf()
_bottomRow.ccmShape: kind 'message': { roots (the union members to try), namePath, descPath, colorPath + colorMap, symbolPath, idPath, typePath, clearIds }: shared/hud.js ccMsgOf(). The older kinds 'list' and 'flag' (car3 I) still work.
_bottomRow.roadShape: { iface, field, instance, path, textKey, spacerKey, iconKey, iconTextKey, spacerMap, maxLen }: shared/hud.js roadOf(). The icon's own picture is a navigation resource handle we cannot resolve, so only its text is used; the road shields come later (docs/ROAD-SHIELDS.md).
_bottomRow.navShape: { iface, instance, state: { field, path, map }, next: { field, distPath, unitPath, unitMap, etaPath, timePath }, here: { field, validPath, streetPath, cityPath } }. 'here' is the car's position: PERSONAL DATA, read only as a fallback road label, never logged, never sent anywhere.

sign._values: The raw speed values follow the convention of the car's own FASuS NextClassLimitSpeed enum, which is the only one in the catalogue that spells them out: 0 = AUFHEBUNG_ALLES (the end of all restrictions, the derestriction sign), 254 = NICHT_VERFUEGBAR and 255 = SIGNAL_UNBEFUELLT (no limit known, BMW's empty sign). displaySpeedLimit itself is a plain UInt8 with no names, so this is reasoning, not proof: the 'sign:' log line on the car settles it. "none" is empty on purpose - the owner's cluster essentially always shows a sign (2026-11-15).
sign._hold: The stock cluster animates the end of a limit and then shows the new one, and a sign is essentially always present (the owner, 2026-11-15), so there is no "hide the sign" state. holdMs keeps the last sign on while the car briefly says nothing; the animation itself lands in shared/hud.js _signShow().
sign._timings: changeFlashMs / flashPeriodMs are docs/G20-DESIGN-SPEC.md's PLACEHOLDERS for the flash after a limit changes - there is no video in the reference set, so nothing was measured. They are parameters only; nothing acts on them yet.
sign._empty: docs/G20-DESIGN-SPEC.md: BMW's empty sign is THREE DASHES, 8.8 x 4.4 at pitch 13, not a blank disc. That is WBSIGN's u_show state 3, which this package already drives; whether the shader draws dashes is the drawing package's to check.
sign._mph: The unit is read and recorded ({{limitUnit}}, the 'sign:' log line) but changes nothing on screen: the sign stays the round one with the number, in every country (the owner, 2026-11-15).
sign._tsr: car-fix CF2 (the car session of 2026-11-18): the field above never arrives on the owner's car (its provider never comes up); the limit comes as the EVENT de.bmw.dass.TrafficSignRecognition.TrafficSignRecognition (service 13632, instance 1, about 2 a second): presentClassLimitSpeed x 5 = km/h (class 8 with a 40 sign, 6 with a 30, 10 = 50 in town). shared/limit_src.js reads it into the same sign shape; 'order' says which source speaks first while it is live (the event, then this field as the fallback; an event older than staleMs is not live). 'none' classes draw no sign: 0 (FASuS's AUFHEBUNG_ALLES), 29 (its chime request, not a speed), 253..255 (n/a, unfilled); warnMap: controlSLIWarning 0 / 1 seen, 1 = over the limit is a hypothesis; mph: unitOfMeasurementSpeedLimit 1 = MPH by FASuS's enum, anything else km/h; endOn (presentWithdrawalLimitSpeed values that mean the derestriction sign; 2 = AUFHEBUNG by the enum) is empty until the car shows one. 'camera' (the front camera's own event) is a witness: logged ('limit: camera ...'), never drawn.

ccm._timings: PARAMETERS ONLY - nothing acts on them, except autoHideMs since 0.7.20 (config.ccActive.fallback, the ccList heuristic while statusActiveCCMessage has not spoken). This package builds STATES, not animations (the owner, 2026-11-15): a message appears and disappears with no flash. ccFrameDwellMs is docs/G20-DESIGN-SPEC.md's guess at how long one frame of a cycling message is shown, which we do not need because the car says which frame it is on itself (config.ccFrames). autoHideMs / reshowMs are BMW's manual's ~20 s auto-hide and ~8 s hide-then-reshow. They live here so animation can be added later without touching the drawing.
ccm._colour: White only for now (the owner, 2026-11-15): cCColor is read and recorded but every message is drawn in the theme's normal foreground. The seam is one line - put "colorBy": "cc" back on the cc_name text in design/gen_6wb.py cc_row(), which turns on shared/hud.js _ccRole().

sla._about: The driver's own speed-limit settings (read only). The red arc on our speed scale follows the car's own excess-speed verdict instead of comparing speed against the sign ourselves: displaySpeedLimitWarning in the sign struct says WHEN the car considers the driver over, and "warn" below says whether the driver asked for that warning at all. The offsets are the tolerance the driver set; we do not need them to draw, and they are read for the log so the car's behaviour can be understood.
sla._readonly: Nothing here is ever written. The fields are "rws" on the car; app.json declares them "s", so our generated interface config has neither a setter nor a getter. The values arrive by notification only - see the note beside the interface in "signals" for why the getter had to go.

parts.note: THIS is the field taken as "the excess-speed display is on"

ccFrames._about: Which frame of how many the stock cluster is showing. docs/G20-DESIGN-SPEC.md: the car CYCLES NUMBERED FRAMES, it does not stack or side-scroll, and this field is how it says so. When it arrives, our text follows the car's frame exactly instead of running its own clock.

config._ccMarker: Strip integration, the owner's decision 7 (2026-11-16): BMW's marker right of its check-control panel (none / warning triangle / 'i') is COVERED in every lane of the strip mask and in both modes. It may open only while a CONFIRMED signal says BMW draws it: set ccMarker to { iface, field, path?, shownWhen?: [raw values meaning shown] } (shared/hud.js _markShown) and bake the mask with its marker lanes (tools/strip/bake_mask.py --marker). No such signal is confirmed (ccList is the candidate, docs/strip/P-REPORT.md 1.1), so it stays null.

ccActive._about: fix/active-cc (0.7.20), the owner's car 2026-11-17: ccList lists the ACTIVE AND THE STORED messages - a ready-to-drive message (id 987) stayed listed after BMW hid it (~20 s), so 0.7.19 kept our message area open / drawn with nothing of BMW's on screen. This field, KombiIF statusActiveCCMessage, is taken as the cluster's own 'message shown now' (a HYPOTHESIS until the car confirms it). Every change is logged once, numbers only: 'active cc: number N control C frame F/G utility U'. Once it has notified with a number ('wired') it alone decides: a message shows iff numberPath is not in noneValues; text, colour and severity come from the ccList entry whose cCIdentifer equals that number. No such entry: still shown, BMW's panel stays open, our line empty, and 'active cc: no ccList entry for number N' is logged once per N - that line tells whether the two numberings match. The catalogue default of the number is 65535 (unfilled); it is NOT in noneValues, so it reads as shown with no entry: BMW's panel open (the safe side). shared/hud.js _ccListEval.
ccActive._fallback: A HEURISTIC, used only while statusActiveCCMessage has never given a number: a ccList entry counts as showing for hideAfterMs (null: config.ccm.autoHideMs, 20000 - BMW's manual's ~20 s auto-hide) after it was first listed; an entry whose colour is in keepColors shows for as long as it is listed. An entry that leaves the list and comes back starts its clock again. on: false gives back 0.7.19 (every listed entry shows while listed).
ccActive._release: research3/mc (docs/research3/MC-REPORT.md), OFF while absent: 0.7.20 exactly. When set, an object {deferValues, deferControls, leftList, noEntryMs, witness, then} that says when the 'shown now' value is NO VERDICT, and the list then decides - then 'listed' (default: shown while ccList lists any entry outside ignoreIds, never closes over a listed message) or 'heuristic' (the fallback above). The report's recommended value for the next install, after the log read: {"deferValues": [65535], "leftList": true}. noEntryMs can hide a message ccList never carries (case S5) and is not recommended. Every change logs 'active cc: released to the list (...)' once, numbers only. shared/hud.js _ccRelease. car-fix CF1: it acts on the ACTIVE number only - obsolete with source displayed (Діагностика 'Release a stuck check-control message' still writes it; it acts only with the 'shown now' source setting on 'active').

ccList._about: Several messages at once: the car cycles through this list, and ours steps through it on the same clock (the owner, 2026-11-15). Each element carries a short name and a colour; config.ccm.cycleMs is how long each one is shown. The stock order and timing are being measured in docs/G20-DESIGN-SPEC.md.
ccList._cclist: fix/cclist (0.7.19), the owner's car 2026-11-17: newCCMessage (config.ccm) sent NOTHING in 25 minutes, a door-open message included; ccList is live and carries the message on show. Resting: [id 0 GREEN symbol 6]; driver's door open: [id 15 WHITE symbol 2], name 16 characters; shut: id 0 again. So THIS is the primary source of 'a message shows' (an entry whose cCIdentifer is not in ignoreIds - from ONE test, hence configurable) and of our message's headline (cCShortName), colour and severity (cCColor) and symbol id (cCListSymbolID). newCCMessage stays wired as a second source; whichever says a message shows wins. The first notification that is a list whose entries fit 'root' ends the blind case (hud.js _ccWired). Member names from the catalogue: CCListElementUnion.cCListElement = CCListElementStruct { cCIdentifer (sic), cCShortName, cCListSymbolID, cCColor, cCIndentation, ricResourceID }. The text is never logged.

here._about: PERSONAL DATA. The street is used only as a fallback road label; the coordinates only for the sunrise and sunset that drive the night colours (the owner, 2026-11-15), falling back to config.location when the position is not valid. Neither is ever logged or sent anywhere.

_car3.driveShape: { iface, field, path: [..], map: { '<raw>': 'COMFORT' | 'COMFORT_PLUS' | 'SPORT' | 'SPORT_PLUS' | 'ECO_PRO' | 4 ... } }: the drive mode from another field than FES statusFESVehicleDynamicSwitchHMI (which gave nothing on the owner's car); the value goes through the same handler, so layout choice is unchanged. null: that FES field only.
_car3.about: Package I (docs/CAR3-I-REPORT.md). Fields not known yet, so null: then nothing is subscribed. ./scripts/car_signals.sh root@<car> ranks the car's catalogue for each and prints these lines; each interface must also go under signals (flag s, or rs with a getter). Every new raw value is logged once ('msa raw', 'clock raw', 'check-control raw') to calibrate.
_car3.msaShape: { iface, field, path: [..], map: { '<raw>': 'active' | 'off' | 'stopped' | 'unavailable' | null } }: our auto start/stop sign in the 6WB layouts (hidden while active or unmapped; green while MSA has stopped the engine, the rev needle at READY; crossed out while off or unavailable)
_car3.clockShape: { iface, field, kind: 'offset', path: [..], factor (1: minutes, 60: hours, 1/60: seconds), dstPath: [..] + dstMinutes (60), invalid: [..] } or { iface, field, kind: 'local', hourPath: [..], minutePath: [..] }: the car's time zone for our clock, the FIRST source (package X), then the timeZone setting, then utcOffsetMinutes
_car3.ccmShape: { iface, field, kind: 'list', path: [..] (a message shows while the array is not empty) } or { iface, field, kind: 'flag', path: [..], on: [..] | off: [..] (default [0, false]) }: hud.js _raw('ccMsg'), for 6WB Dials + G20's hooks

_limit.about: Package E (docs/POLISH-E-REPORT.md). The speed-limit and no-overtaking signs' data source is not known yet: no public MGU app reads one, so limit / nopass stay null. Then the car shows no sign of ours (the demo drive shows 90) and 6WB Dials + G20 keeps its window over BMW's sign open. Once a field is named here and under signals, our sign is the only one: that window stays closed, black while the car has sent nothing.
_limit.find: ./scripts/car_signals.sh root@<car> copies /etc/oap/someip/someip-interfaces.json once (read only: cat) and ranks its fields for limit, nopass, msa, clock and ccm with tools/signals/catalog.py; it prints the signals entry and a config line for the best of each (docs/CAR3-I-REPORT.md).
_limit.limitShape: { iface, field, path: [..] (into the value), factor (1), unit: 'kmh' | 'mph', unitPath: [..] + mph: [raw unit values meaning mph], invalid: [raw: no limit known], end: [raw: end of limit / unlimited], map: { '<raw>': kmh | 'end' | 'unknown' | null } (enum fields), min (5), max (250); car3 I: unknown: [raw: BMW's empty sign '---', Speed Limit Info on but no limit known], statePath: [..] + stateMap: { '<raw>': 'unknown' | 'none' | 'end' | 'limit' } (a separate state member) }
_limit.nopassShape: { iface, field, path: [..], on: [raw values meaning no overtaking] (default [1, true]) }
candidates: 1. A field named after BMW's own words for the feature. The ID4-6 car data service names them driving.sliActualSpeedLimitInfo (601), driving.sliNextSpeedLimitRecognition (600), driving.sliTextMessage (599), driving.trafficSignInfo1..4 (591-594), driving.trafficSignInfoVisibility (595), driving.orInfo (598), driving.orNPITextMessage (597, No Passing Info), driving.signRecognitionFrontCamera (605): BimmerGestalt/IDriveConnectKit core/src/commonMain/kotlin/io/bimmergestalt/idriveconnectkit/CDSProperty.kt lines 176-190. Not MGU SOME/IP names: tools/signals/catalog.py greps the car's catalogue for SLI, NPI, trafficSign, speedLimit, overtaking, orInfo, signRecognition.

2. Navigation map data, only while a route runs: de.bmw.infotainment.navigation.guiding.GuidanceEventList queryContent, union members speedLimit / speedLimitAssist and speedLimitAssistInfo on each event (cauliflowermossgrape/idrive7-apps apps/redline/nav.js line 134, kit/tools/fixtures/redline-nav-carplay-2026-11-09.txt: speedLimitAssistInfo {nil: NO_VALUE} on a CarPlay route). Upcoming limits, not the sign in force; a method, not a field: not usable as config.limit as is.

3. Unverified guess: a field of the cluster's or the HUD's own data (KombiIF / KombiInterface_2 already carry the cluster's range and check-control list). If the head unit draws BMW's HUD content (cluster-render's HUD target suggests it can), its catalogue must carry the sign; the name is unknown.

diag._about: B7, the Діагностика menu (screen DIAG, shared/diag_settings.js): each setting writes the config paths named here while it is ON (all OFF by default = the keys as this file has them, put back when a setting goes off). A path is dotted; a choice lists its options. car-fix CF1: diagShownNow 'active' gives back 0.7.20's 'shown now' source (it replaced research3/MC's diagDisplayed, whose witness is the source now). The values are the ones the research3 reports and their test files name (tools/research3/mb/exp/f30-gap.json).

menu.comment: The centre screen's native menu (shared/menu.js). hideModeRows: hide In Comfort / In Sport / In Eco Pro while Change with the drive mode is off (the RHMI Visible property, not yet seen on the car; false keeps them always shown). hideRowUnlessG20: hide 'Bottom row while G20 shows' in the Settings list while the g20 toggle is off, the same property and the same caveat; false keeps it always shown, which costs nothing either way - with G20 off our background covers BMW's row, so the setting is inert then (hud.js _own).
